card.intuition: Clearing ends the current session and starts a fresh one, so the next message begins with an empty context window. The model is stateless, so none of the old session's working state carries over — a clean cure for a polluted context full of failed attempts and stale tool results. The transcript usually stays on disk to read or resume; only the agent's working state is gone.
card.analogy: Rebooting a wedged server: instead of fighting through corrupted state, you kill the process and start clean, pointing the config at the same files on restart.
card.time_complexity: The model is stateless, so each handoff forces the next session to re-read everything needed from context — carried material costs tokens on every request.
card.space_complexity: The context window is finite, and clearing frees the entire budget at once by dropping everything; the new session starts with zero footprint.
when_to_use: When a session is stuck looping on a failing test and prodding does not help
When the agent is ignoring instructions because accumulated noise has diluted them
Before starting new work, once important decisions have been written to a handoff artifact
gotchas: Nothing carries over, including real progress — write a handoff artifact first if the next session needs those decisions
The model is stateless, so the new session knows nothing the old one knew
Clearing is the blunter tool than compaction: it drops the junk, but it also drops everything worth keeping

steps.label: Bad context
steps.annotation: A long session accumulates failed attempts and wrong turns that the model re-reads on every turn.

steps.label: Drop context
steps.annotation: The user clears the session, ending its working state entirely.

steps.label: Fresh session
steps.annotation: The next message begins with an empty session and an empty context window.

steps.label: Re-point at docs
steps.annotation: The user starts the new session pointing at the plan doc and the test file.

steps.label: Transcript kept
steps.annotation: The harness usually keeps the history on disk, so it can be read or resumed even though the agent's working state is gone.
